item.title: Re: Reanimation SCP - Seeking Greenlights
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for crit
– hide block

The Crystal is sentient, and an entity inhabits it.

This is the first the crystal is mentioned and it's not exactly clear what it's role is here: I'm assuming it's the thing that actually does the reanimation?

and it's eventually discovered he is not who he says he is.

who is he? the implication i'm getting here is that it doesn't really matter cos the focus after this switches to the crystal but?

It's a demonic entity trapped within the Crystal, reduced to a parasite, feeding off life-energy to survive.

My concern with this big reveal here is that it feels like it'd produce a reaction best described as 'okay but so what?'

I think my big concern with this is it's structured like a series of big reveals but none of the reveals feel like they have real narrative weight: the problem is that a lot of the time, the reveal doesn't really significantly change our understanding of what's happening. Like, consider the hivemind reveal: we find out it's a parasitic life form and our reaction then is 'huh that's weird' but there's not really any further implications from there? This is in part because it's entire motivation is 'trying to survive', which like, everything does; as opposed to like, trying to achieve a specific aim.

It also feels like it really needs to tap into some kinda primal fear or emotion here: like, if this was centred around the fear of being replaced or something, it'd end up feeling a lot more impactful to me. As it is, there feels like this has a real lack of emotional response here: all of this happens but it never feels like it's impactful.

item.title: Re: The Tower (XVI)
item.content:encoded:
Hey there again Oystershell, let's take a look at your edits!

+ Open
- Close

So your idea's essentially the same, but you've explained it more specifically, which is good. I also like the idea of a complex game of seeing-but-not-seeing the future you've created (i.e predicting the future, but only really vaguely), along with the added complexity behind the Tower card seeing visions of the end of the world.

Unfortunately, this brings up a logistical problem: do the cards predict an absolute future (no matter what you do that future will come to pass) or a likely future? If it's the former, it has implications on timelines and free will (mostly Fatalism/Hard Determinism), and if it's the latter then seeing the cards might alter the most likely possible future (due to interpretations of them). I think I might be overthinking this, but you may want to consider this.

One last thing: some of the more skeptical members of this Site don't like seeing Thaumiel SCPs created by the Foundation that the Foundation has a disproportionate amount of trust in (considering they're still anomalies), especially ones as borderline OP as this one. It can be viewed as cliche (especially when they fail epically, as this one did), and can serve to break the suspension of disbelief for some of the readers on the Site. To remedy this, I'd recommend contacting some reviewers from the Butterfly Squad to get some alternative opinions on your concept, as my opinion is simply one of many.

Anyway, thanks for reading, and I hope this helps!
P.S For future reference, the one-sentence summary in my previous crit is there to help you get a view on the very basics that critters see when they read your concept, and thus help you get a more objective/wide look at your idea to see if you want to change anything.
P.P.S Damn that was a long sentence.
P.P.P.S Ok I'll stop bothering you now.

item.title: Re: Axolotl
item.content:encoded:
Hey there Choysis, I'll be critting your idea today!
Note that I am neither a particularly experienced nor an offical reviewer, so take what I say with a grain of salt. With that being said, let's begin the crit!

+ Open Section-by-Section +
- Close Section-by-Section -

Elevator Pitch

So it's a celestial guardian of Earth (or rather, humanity) that lives in its own dimension, and the twist is that it's an axolotl? I'll be honest, I don't really like this idea, and as a general rule I'd advise staying away from supreme cosmic beings that defend Earth, as they're viewed as cliche by popular opinion on this Site. The axolotl part also just feels random and janky, and doesn't really fit in with the whole 'cosmic guardian' idea. In short, I think this idea is a cliche 'cosmic guardian entity', but the only flavour being that it's an axolotl for some reason (which feels random and forced).

Central Narrative

Unfortunately, your narrative isn't very impressive either, just basically a highlight reel of how the axolotl has been spotted throughout history and either stopped entities capable of K-Class scenarios1, or accidentally caused collateral damage, with minimum damage to humans. The part about the paintings and carvings makes sense however, nice catch there.

Hook/Attention Grabber

Is this idea fun or funny? I'd have to say no. It just feels kind of inane and random, assigning the role of almighty cosmic guardian to an axolotl.

+ Open General Thoughts +
- Close General Thoughts -

As a general rule, one should stay away from almighty, nigh-omnipotent beings as SCPs (very few articles get away with this. Actually, I think there's only one that does), especially ones that only exist to protect humanity from other SCPs. It just seems cliche, and, with the axolotl part, kind of random and silly.

I'd recommend three things:
1. Consider overhauling your idea (maybe making it a bit less OP and/or random) and/or story
2. Check out the Guide Hub for great advice on ideation, story writing, and more!
3. Contact reviewers from the Butterfly Squad for alternative opinions from experienced reviewers

And finally, to sum up your idea in one sentence2:
A cosmic, all-powerful axolotl that lives in its own dimension, emerging only to engage with and stop entities causing K-Class events.

Anyway, that's it for my crit today. Thanks for reading, and I hope this helps!

Footnotes
1. Being nitpicky here, but there is no way the Foundation names an anomaly, especially one capable of causing K-Class events, "Lil' Devil". This serves to break the suspension of disbelief of readers, something that articles should try their best to maintain (this is, although fictional, a scientific organisation after all).
2. This is to give you a quick idea of what critters see when they read your idea, and thus make it easier to see what you do or don't like.

item.title: Re: Monster maker
item.content:encoded:
Hey there Researcher Penguin, I'll be critting your idea today!
Note that I am neither a particularly experienced nor official reviewer, so take everything I say with a grain of salt. With that said, let's begin the crit!

+ Open Section-by-Section +
- Close Section-by-Section -

Elevator Pitch

Ok, so your concept is an amusement park run by a British businessman with a bunch of anomalous creatures of all shapes and sizes contained in habitats for viewing, however, it's all a lure to bring people in to turn them into more anomalous creatures. Unfortunately, I can't say I'm very keen on this idea, as it isn't very original (just a parade of random monsters displayed for people to see) or interesting (see previous point) and lacks substance (i.e a good story).

Central Narrative

Central Narrative: none

Yikes. Narrative is almost a necessity for every article nowadays (Series VI), and it's come to be expected that all the newer articles have something at least resembling a story (and if not, an extremely strong premise, which this isn't). Without story, your idea just… falls flat on its face. There isn't anything interesting here, just a weird monster amusement park to be locked away and never seen again. This may have been acceptable in Series I, but not anymore. I'd suggest brainstorming a story before you continue with ideation, as this is one of the most vital parts of not only yours but any SCP.

Hook/Attention Grabber

You have an okay hook (anomalous businessmen with many anomalous creatures at their back), but as I stated previously, your idea collapses without a story to back it up. Work on the story first.

+ Open General Thoughts +
- Close General Thoughts -

Hate to sound like a broken record, but story is what you need here. If you're planning on continuing this idea, then work on the story, the backbone of your article, first. Think of a genre (horror, dramatic, mystery, etc.), think of what you want your readers to feel, then try and build a narrative off of that1.

I'll recommend two more things while I'm here:
1. Check out the Guide Hub for some great tips and essays on everything, from building stories to pacing articles and more!
2. Reach out to reviewers on the Butterfly Squad for some alternative opinions and advice from experienced reviewers!

And finally, to sum up your idea in one sentence2:
An amusement park full of wildly varying anomalous creatures, run by an anomalous businessmen who uses it to lure humans in and turn them into more anomalous creatures.

Anyway, that's it for my crit today. Thanks for reading, and I hope this helps!

Footnotes
1. I know this is vague, but creative ideation is an esoteric business that differs for everyone, and this works for me.
2. This is to give you an idea of the bare bones of what a reviewer sees from your concept, thereby giving you the opportunity to change it accordingly.

item.title: First Time Idea - No-Tell Motel
item.content:encoded:
The idea is for an SCP that is a roadside motel in the Arizona desert. This motel is a fixed point in multiple realities. The different worlds can be viewed from the different room's windows. The inside is infinitely bigger inside than outside, and labyrinthine. Examples include a barren white world of perpetual night, at the bottom of an alien ocean, an alien swamp, and etc. Creatures and other entities can break through the windows from time to time. There appears to be no staff, until those who are drawn to enter it "check out" the next day. The staffs' features can never be remembered by those that observe them. It is Euclid class, and fenced off with posted guards. Yet, still, sometimes civilians and even a guard or two, somehow, manage to enter.

item.title: Monster maker
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: There is an amusement park containing various creatures led by a British businessman, the monsters very wildly ranging from literal planet consuming monsters to sentient bug-like creatures all contained and safe for viewing, it being encouraged to observe them in their "habitats". The habitats are unusually fitted for the creature at hand with the supplies for upkeep never seen. The British businessman himself is the only one there seemingly doing everything there being everywhere in the park. The monsters at the park however were once humans. When the Businessman gets bored of the current attractions he lures people selecting three interesting individuals and giving them free items. These items slowly transform the person into one a monster before being brought in by him to display.

Central Narrative: none

Hook/Attention-Grabber: It presents the foundation with a large amount of anomalous creatures all relatively safe with the main concern being its owner and manager the buisnessman

Additional Notes: I haven't yet decided if the man will have a known identity. I'm still pondering if what to keep mystified about the man and his attractions. suggestions are very welcome.

item.title: Re: On the Shores of Paradise
item.content:encoded:
So I had an idea if I'm going to make this a part of the Competitive Eschatology. I've also decided to focus on a couple of protagonists here (through transcripts and emails, as both of them are high-ranking scientists).

+ Open Protagonists
- Close Protagonsists

Both protagonists are close friends, but here is where their opinions split. This will act as the turning point that fractures their relationship.

Protagonist 1 - For evacuating people into Paradise
Has lost many people to the calamity that is Competitive Eschatology, including close friends and family members. Wants to see a bright future where no one has to suffer any more, and sees Paradise as a way to embody that future for everyone. Argues that Paradise seems completely harmless and is in fact beneficial for us. Ends up going into Paradise after a last, emotional goodbye to their friend.

Protagonist 2 - Against evacuating people into Paradise
Has also lost people to Competitive Eschatology, including family and close friends. Wants to stop the suffering all over the world, but doesn't want to use anomalies out of distrust. Argues that 'Paradise' is incredibly suspicious in how it seems to be constructed for our desires. Ends up seeing their friend off into Paradise, but not entering it themselves.

+ Open Big Reveal
- Close Big Reveal

Big argument between everyone (Ethics Committee, the protagonists, etc.) on whether the use of this is ethically acceptable. Eventually, increasing pressure makes the Foundation use Paradise to evacuate a whole bunch of civilians (Veil be damned) and some scientists and members of the Foundation. Once the last person comes through (one of the protagonists), all of the wildlife goes quiet, the weather stops and becomes neutral rather than perfect, and the protagonist in Paradise walks on while the protagonist seeing their friend off realises something bad is happening and tries to leap into Paradise to save their friend. They don't make it in time.

An omnipresent voice speaks out, saying 'thank you for the sacrifices', and shuts the gate, before all hell breaks loose on the beach (the animals change, the fungi and plants begin spreading, the weather changes). The protagonist outside Paradise has most of their dominant arm cut off, and is left on the beach.

The beach changes into a hostile landscape inhabited by dangerous flora and fauna that quickly begin spreading, converting all the land they spread across into more of what is at the beach (foggy and misty, cold, numerous symbols everywhere on the plants, animals, and land).

While the protagonist is dying on the beach watching everything around them turn horrible, another entity appears on the beach. They have a brief conversation where the entity introduces itself as a primordial nature spirit attracted by the happenings on Earth as a means to gain power through sacrifices. The protagonist is understandably extremely angry, but the entity says that they won't be angry for much longer and walks off. Here, the protagonist dies.

There is then an updated version of the document that reflects the recent changes that occurred, along with updates on what is going on.

To sum up the big reveal, the entity used the Paradise gateway as a means to get a bunch of sacrifices to increase its power (and harvest more sacrifices). It wants to spread itself as far as possible, and once it gets the sacrifices it uses them to change the beach into basically a spreading land virus that converts the land it touches into more of the spirit's domain to get even more sacrifices through victims.

Dunno if it's cliche or not, but I thought it fit the theme of Competitive Eschatology (specifically 'awakening'). Hope this is satisfactory!

item.title: "Now thats what I call existence"
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Comedy, Existential Happiness

Elevator Pitch: An unmarked CD that can transport any listener to a seemingly infinite hall like room. The room is covered in forms of digital media, every piece being some form of strange variation of the cd "Now that's what I call music Vol 1!".

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: SCP researchers and class D personal are transported to the collection room and are greeted by a sign that hangs off of a rail attached to the ceiling of this room that spans the full length. The sign moves into view, all that is said on the sign is "Welcome, and enjoy my collection." The Article will be split into two parts mainly, with the researchers walking down the hall and noting interesting deviations with certain items in the collection. Examples include "That's what I call actor Andy Warhol's face Vol 1!" and "That's what I call just Hoobastank Vol 1!".

The second section would detail the research teams further dives into the hall. After multiple hours of walking they come to another sign hanging from a rail, this sign precedes more of the hall but every shelf past this sign is empty. The sign proclaims that the rest of the hall is dedicated to alternate universe versions of earth that have not yet made their respective version of "That's what I call music Vol 1!". The sign then begins to wax poetic about how no matter the horrific world or terrifying problems humanity may fall under, almost every single version of humanity has had it in them to at *least* make one version of "Now that's what I call music Vol 1!". The collection is a testament to humanities capacity to at least make this one cd every time.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The foundation never actually sees the being behind the collection, and Nothing actually dangerous happens to the researchers, its just a strange walk through a weird "turtles all the way down" style museum

Additional Notes: This is my first real scp idea that I've put any weight into actually writing about and I made this post for the critique it needs but also just to make sure that this idea isn't something that has already been made. Thank you for reading

item.title: Re: Reanimation SCP - Seeking Greenlights
item.content:encoded:
I never had any intention to piggyback of someone else's work. 2718 is one of my favourite SCPs, and during writing the draft, I thought it'd be a cool way to pay homage to it.

It's not about what your intentions are, but how it will appear. Also paying homage to another skip as your first skip is a bad look. Make something your own and have the article stand on its own as much as you possibly can.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:

This section is exactly the same as it used to be and does not reflect the current iteration of the concept.

Overall:
my concern here is the tired trope of the cult leader, not that you can't do a skip about a cult… I have and many others have, but what sets your cult apart? What is the cult's philosophy? Also what is the twist with the cult leader? You say he's not what he seems to be… but then don't explain.

Are the reainimated people still extensions of himself? like the crystal? Did he make a hive mind? What's he turning these people into?

What's the overall tone you are looking for? What themes are you going to be looking at? Or is this: plainly spooky cult make makes zombies?

item.title: Re: *Seeking Greenlight* Mu-13-C "Cats Eye"
item.content:encoded:
So mostly I am on board with this. But there a few things I think need work:

1) layout: how is your article to be structured? How will you communicate these things to your reader logistically? If it were a tale this is easy, but as an SCP, you have to not only follow formatting but also use the formatting in an engaging way. For example, I dislike endless journal entries unless they are written in a punchy and interesting way… the same goes for test logs.

2) I am a cat person, so take this with love…. but I can't imagine a cat doing what its told if its life depended on it. So these cats can see spectral entities… but how could the MTF or field researchers utilize the cats to do so? Not like cats are gonna be responding to voice commands the way dogs usually do… unless they were trained dramatically I'd guess.

3) perspective: Who's perspective is this from? As cute as the cats are, it will be hard to relate to the cats as characters

item.title: Re: SCP Article Concept: The Disposal Squid (Seeking Greenlights)
item.content:encoded:
Alright, let's consider these in order.

  1. I'm not so sure how much this would solve your ambiguity problem. It still doesn't explain the disparity between your description of the object and its potential effects.
  2. How would that resolve the story? You'd still have those two missing people, and I don't see how that ability would quite make sense when combined with the anomaly's existing qualities.
  3. That could hypothetically work, but it would need a rehashing of the story to make the goo a more central aspect, in my view. I'm also not seeing a thematic connection between the core anomaly and the goo.
  4. There are certainly ways to incorporate it. The narrative just needs to be tweaked to utilize it properly.

Actual Spoilers
– hide block

That's the body of my problem. What this was supposed to be, is a Deep State version of the Foundation. They hid the documentation within the normal listings (Plain Sight) and they've been designing this organism and infecting the world with it. I don't know how it would be possible to state that without actually stating that, which would defeat the point of them operating in secrecy.

The "puzzle" isn't so much about that, as it is just simply that it's old Dr. Kondraki in charge of this program now, and he's plotting (successfully, at this point) to take over not just the Foundation, but the world itself, by using this to make people produce butterfly pheromones. But honestly, I didn't care if that part came through to everyone - that was just an Easter Egg for the hell of it. The main point was supposed to be the above paragraph. There's no anomaly here, there's nothing weird going on at all, except that a bunch of scientists are intentionally fucking up human biology for the sake of their version of the "greater good." Since this is inevitably going to fail, I'll stick it back in my sandbox when it does and pull it back later if I can figure out a way to rework it so the "Deep State" bit is more obvious. I just feel like, by doing so, it kind of makes it not a "Deep State" and thus less intrinsically sinister.

item.title: Re: How to add Audio to an SCP
item.content:encoded:
You can view the Page Source of the article via the "+ Options" link at the bottom of the page, to see the code needed to insert the audio. You'd upload the audio file to the page the article is on, and use the wikidot code from the page you're using as an example.

That said, it's highly recommended that you get the concept reviewed before you start working on a full draft, so you can be relatively certain that what you have in mind will be well-received by the audience. If you immediately start recording/editing the audio and the audience isn't that interested in the concept, that means a lot more redos and legwork.
